label: early original-phase input o/w/0/a following u/w/0/o/g/2/b
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t >= 1) & (t <= 3) & isin(in_tok, [tok("o"), tok("w"), tok("0"), tok("a")]) & isin(prev_tok, [tok("u"), tok("w"), tok("0"), tok("o"), tok("g"), tok("2"), tok("b")])
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at early positions: t=1-4 carry 93% of activations and 95% of mass, t=1 is strongest, and it never fires at t=0. Delimiter and copy phases hold under 5% of mass. Within that window it depends on the current input token (o, w, 0, a give 6.8x/6.3x/5.7x/3.3x lift and about 77% of mass; i, t, g, c are weaker) together with the preceding token (u, w, 0, o, g, 2, b raise the rate). The first token also matters (u is 4.3x). So it behaves like a conjunctive code over the first few tokens rather than a single token detector. Requiring both the current-token set and the previous-token set gives dev precision 0.53 and recall 0.39 (F1 0.45, mass recall 0.57). Position plus current token alone gives recall 0.64 but precision 0.20. The biggest activations (e.g. b u [w][0], b u u [a], u u [o]) come at t=1-3 with these token combinations. It rarely fires on digits 1/2 as input, on repeated tokens (in_first=0 is 0.3x), or on late original positions (t>=5).
